Fifteen years later I showed it to Dante Buzzetti who identified it as an 'ensaio de canto' (half song) of Turdus rufiventris or T. amaurochalinus, probably the former. I have changed the ID to Turdus rufiventris, ID questioned.

I'd like to identify the bird behind the singing. Recording is unedited, it's exactly how it was. Bird starts singing from 0:05 seconds. 

In background we can hear some sparrows but the singing sounds pretty clear.  This birds sang during all the day from the morning to the evening. 

It's a country area so there are a lot of birds. However I  never heard that singing before in 18 years I lived there. 

Thanks a lot in advance!
